counter_evidence:
The claim's own falsifier is met. Presence-polarity probes from the panel's designs pass their control pairs, then return PRESENT (applies) after harmless moves and rewordings. I ran every probe below read-only in node over `git show` blobs with in-memory overlays (script: C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-User-Documents-projects-EMS-workshop1--claude-worktrees-knowledge-store-research-9c609c\f3bbe503-2a20-4258-976b-7d457d3bf63a\scratchpad\probes.mjs).

(1) ex1, B-style and design-style probe: `compare_digest[(]` over backend/app/**/*.py, excluding core/security.py and identity/security.py.
- Controls: PRESENT at 2fe77f5^ (customer_messaging/router.py:155, customer_messaging/service.py:154, ops/deps.py:42); ABSENT at origin/main.
- Pure file move core/security.py -> core/secrets.py, no text change: PRESENT(backend/app/core/secrets.py:34). That is the guard itself (compare_secret) being moved.
- Moving identity/security.py -> identity/pin_hashing.py: PRESENT(:44).
- So the path allow-list is a location anchor, not a stable semantic anchor (M-03.F12).

(2) ex1, C/D-style count of `hmac.compare_digest(` in the three call-site files.
- Controls: 3 at 2fe77f5^, 0 at origin/main.
- A comment-only edit of ops/deps.py:42 (`# compare_secret, not hmac.compare_digest on str:` -> `...compare_digest(str, str):`) gives PRESENT(1).
- All three files already carry such comments at origin/main (ops/deps.py:42, customer_messaging/router.py:154, customer_messaging/service.py:155), each one character away from matching.

(3) ex3, A-style regex_in_span: anchor `const logPayment = useCallback(`, PRESENT on `crypto.randomUUID()`.
- PRESENT at origin/main (span 312-328), which is correct.
- A correct P12a-shape fix in the repo's own idiom still reads PRESENT (span 312-329). In that fix PaymentModal holds the id and logPayment takes `clientId ?? crypto.randomUUID()`, copying src/features/jobs/data/mapJob.js:199 `client_id: form.clientId ?? crypto.randomUUID()`.
- The naive fix, which the entry warns against, reads ABSENT.
- So the presence probe is wrong on both sides of the fix decision.

(4) ex6, ordered_in_span: the refuted A2 ordering, `verify_pin(` before `is_locked(` inside `login`.
- ABSENT at origin/main.
- A comment-only edit of identity/service.py:91 (`# Deliberately BEFORE verify_pin:` -> `verify_pin():`) gives PRESENT ("refuted fix applied"). That is a spurious do-not-apply stop.

(5) The rule's own target reproduces, so the absence half is real:
- ex4, D-style either-absent form: renaming `_MAX_DISPATCH_EVENT_AGE` alone gives PRESENT.
- ex4, C/judge both-absent form: rename plus a lower-case `insert into dispatch_cursor` gives PRESENT. Postgres keywords are case-insensitive, so this is still the same seed.
- Dependabot `dependency-name: expo-*`: the YAML-equivalent `"expo-*"` gives PRESENT.

(6) The polarity rule is not strictly necessary. A narrower rule blocks the same false positive: an absence probe may return applies only on a tree that does NOT contain the fix commit.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor da988e2 origin/main` is true, so every current tree gets inconclusive, exactly as under the polarity rule.
- 145 of 159 local and remote branches do not contain da988e2, so pre-fix trees exist where an absence probe is honest.

(7) ex4 has no presence-polarity text probe at all. Its root-cause line `DispatchCursor(consumer=consumer, last_seq=0)` (backend/app/features/jobs/service.py:501) is present at both da988e2^ and origin/main. Its only declarative discriminator is therefore absence-of-guard.
trace: n/a (not confirmed). The part that holds: the absence half is real. Absence-of-guard text probes (ex4, Dependabot) return applies after a rename, a lower-casing or YAML re-quoting. Historical controls at fails_at/passes_at (X-02.F29) cannot catch this, because the vacuity exists only on the current tree. So some restriction on absence probes is needed. The polarity rule is one; an ancestry gate is another.
narrowed_claim:
What survives:
- The polarity rule blocks the absence-of-guard subclass of reworded-guard false positives, which I reproduced on ex4 and on the Dependabot ignore line. It is not sufficient, because presence probes over source text are fooled by file moves (ex1 path allow-list), comment edits (ex1 count, ex6 ordering) and correct fixes written in a different idiom (ex3). It is also not strictly necessary, because an ancestry gate gives the same protection on post-fix trees.

Every one of the eight has a presence probe or an executable check except ex2's VALIDATE-with-NOT-VALID trap (ex2c). Its condition depends on the deployed head, which is outside the tree (prod_db capability).

Lead eligibility under the rule:
- Lost because of the polarity rule: ex4 (lead only through the Docker db_probe or pytest), ex8's Dependabot sibling (needs a dep_version presence probe instead), and ex2c (A's guard_presence only).
- No text probe in either polarity: ex2b rollback crash-loop (scripted alembic in Docker).
- Docker-only for other reasons: ex5, ex6 and ex1's test id.
- Candidate-only by a separate ruling: ex3. Its presence probe also false-positives after a correct fix.
- Declarative leads without Docker: only ex7 (json_predicate), ex8's plugin probe, ex2a (duplicate_values), and a fragile ex1 count probe.
design_consequence:
Keep KS-A5, but stop presenting it as sufficient. Add these rules:
- (a) **Comment- and string-aware text probes.** regex_in_span and ordered_in_span must match tokens outside comments, docstrings and strings for the file's language. The closed probe set has no such mode today. C already used "non-comment" matching, and its whole-repo grep flipped on comments (4 -> 9).
- (b) **No path allow-lists as the discriminator.** Exclusions must be by symbol, for example "inside the body of the function named compare_secret wherever it lives". That is a stable semantic anchor (M-03.F12).
- (c) **Semantics-preserving mutants at write time and at reaffirm.** Every text probe must stay ABSENT on stored refactor mutants of passes_at: file move, comment edit, identifier rename, YAML quoting, SQL case. Add these as golden negatives in KS-3 alongside C's two naive probes:
  - core/security.py -> core/secrets.py
  - the comment at ops/deps.py:42
  - the comment at identity/service.py:91
  - the mapJob.js:199-idiom ex3 fix
  - Dependabot `"expo-*"`
  - the ex4 rename plus lower-case seed SQL
- (d) **Source-text probes on post-fix trees cap at candidate.** On a tree that contains the entry's fix commit (`merge-base --is-ancestor`), a PRESENT from regex_in_span or ordered_in_span means "regression or refactor": it returns at most candidate unless an executable check agrees. Structured probes over parsed data (json_predicate, duplicate_values, dep_version) keep lead eligibility, which preserves ex7, ex8 and ex2a regression detection.
- (e) **Rewrite §9 known limits and KS-4.** Without Docker, only ex7, ex8's plugin probe, ex2a and (fragile) ex1 can be leads. ex4, ex2b and ex8's Dependabot sibling need executable or dep_version checks. ex2c stays unverified_seed or candidate, since its condition is the deployed head.
